مُطِيبٌ [part. n. of 4: as such signifying] A lawful wedder: a woman said to her beloved, “وَلَا زُرْتَنَا إِلَّا وَأَنْتَ مُطِيبُ
” [Nor didst thou visit us save when thou wast a lawful wedder]: because, in the estimation of excessive lovers, what is unlawful is more sweet. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
